rationales.1: Seasonal shelves, a month filter, and cards that keep sow window, difficulty, price, and stock in fixed corners make per-product reading quick and predictable.
rationales.2: Price and stock occupy consistent card positions, stock language is plain, and the product page runs a fully conventional quantity-plus-basket path; the catalog itself stops at view-this-packet.
rationales.3: The estimated rate is flagged, out-of-stock is shown without hiding the card, the sweet pea says price on request rather than inventing a number, and the UK-only rule sits in a bordered notice at the top of both surfaces.
rationales.4: Single-column cards at phone width, large buttons, and no hover-dependent content serve tablet readers well, though card metadata runs a size smaller than the almanac arm's body text.
rationales.5: The packet-card system with its botanical icons, dashed inner rules, and shelf headers is consistent across surfaces and modes, with only minor internal card-height variance.
rationales.6: The year table, difficulty line, potting-shed note, and companion cards support a confident decision, and the packet illustration adds identity without displacing information.
rationales.7: The rack by the shop door, restocked shelf by shelf by the two owners, is a physical, archetype-true signature that the shelf sections, packet cards, and icon art direction all reinforce.
rationales.8: The rack metaphor and icon illustrations are brand-layer novelty while every checkout-adjacent mechanic stays conventional, exactly inside budget.
rationales.9: Shelf by shelf, two of us keep it stocked carries the neighborly register, though the voice is concentrated in the masthead rather than pervading the entries.
rationales.10: A returning shopper reads season shelves and card-corner stock states at a glance and both surfaces feel like one shop, with no dedicated newly-in surface.
